outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Foundations of Efficient Model Adaptation
outline.description: This chapter establishes the context for parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) in the era of large foundation models. It reviews standard approaches like full fine-tuning, adapter tuning, and prompt tuning, before introducing the specific challenges and motivations behind Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT). Students will understand why preserving geometric relationships (angles) between neurons is crucial for maintaining pre-trained knowledge.
subtopics: The scalability challenge: Training vs. Adapting Foundation Models
Overview of PEFT paradigms: Full Fine-tuning, Adapters, and Prompt Tuning
Geometric principles of fine-tuning: Preserving pairwise angles between neurons
Introduction to Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (OFT): Mechanism and benefits
Limitations of standard OFT: High parameter count and block-diagonal constraints

outline.description: This chapter presents the core theoretical innovation of the paper: reframing matrix factorization as an information transmission problem. Using graph theory concepts, it explains how sparse matrix multiplication can be visualized as signal propagation through a grid-structured network. This framework allows for the systematic design of parameter-efficient dense matrices.
subtopics: Reframing Matrix Factorization: From Algebra to Graph Theory
Visualizing Matrix Multiplication as Information Flow on Grid Graphs
Defining Desiderata: Dense Connectivity vs. Minimum Free Edges
The role of Orthogonality Constraints in Edge Selection
Comparing Sparsity Patterns: Block-Diagonal vs. General Sparse Structures

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Butterfly Structures and Fast Linear Transforms
outline.description: Drawing inspiration from signal processing, this chapter details the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm and its underlying 'butterfly' topology. It explains how this recursive structure enables efficient information mixing with logarithmic complexity ($\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$), providing the blueprint for constructing dense orthogonal matrices with minimal parameters.
subtopics: Historical Context: The Cooley-Tukey FFT Algorithm
Anatomy of the Butterfly Graph Topology
From Signal Processing to Neural Networks: Learning Fast Linear Transforms
Mathematical Definition of Butterfly Factors and Components
Complexity Analysis: Achieving Density with $\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$ Parameters

outline.description: This chapter synthesizes previous concepts to formally define BOFT. It covers the construction of orthogonal butterfly matrices using Cayley parameterization, the recursive definition of block-butterfly components, and practical implementation details such as identity initialization and multiplicative dropout strategies tailored for multiplicative updates.
subtopics: $\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$ Parameterization via Recursive Butterfly Matrices
(Optional) Enforcing Orthogonality via Cayley Transform on Butterfly Blocks
(Optional) Identity Initialization Strategies for Zero-Deviation Startups
(Optional) Designing Multiplicative Dropout for Orthogonal Layers
